# Type System Discipline

Make the compiler reject impossible states, mismatched primitives, and unhandled variants.
Prefer to define errors and special cases out of existence instead of adding handlers.
For TypeScript syntax, see `astack-types` (`astack skill-path astack:types references/typescript-practices.md`).

- Make illegal states unrepresentable. Model variants as sum types: discriminated unions, enums with payloads, or sealed classes. Do not use optional fields that allow contradictory combinations. `{ completed: boolean; completedAt?: Date }` allows `completed: true` without a date. Derive the boolean from `completedAt`. Or model `{ kind: 'open' } | { kind: 'done'; at: Date }`. If a comment must explain valid combinations of fields, split the type into a sum type.
- Construct types from valid values. Do not start with a loose type and remove invalid cases with checks. A non-empty list is a head plus a rest. A valid time range is a start plus a duration. Choose a shape that cannot build the illegal value. Expose the interface that callers need on top.
- Brand semantic primitives. `UserId` and `OrderId` use strings but must not be interchangeable. Give each its own type. Use a branded intersection in TypeScript or a newtype elsewhere. Validate once at creation. Trust the type downstream. If two arguments use the same primitive type for different meanings, brand them.
- External data has no type until parsed. This includes RPC payloads, JSON, IPC messages, CLI args, config files, environment variables, and database rows. At every system edge, parse raw input into the typed model. [Boundary Discipline](boundary-discipline.md) says where to put validation.
- Do not lie to the type system. Casts, unsafe coercions, and assertions that bypass the compiler can cause runtime crashes. If the compiler cannot prove a fact, validate it, narrow it, or refine the model. Otherwise, accept that the cast is a hazard. Trace each `any`, `as`, or `assertNotNull` to the system edge. Validate there.
- Use exhaustive matching. A match on a sum type must fail compilation when a new variant lacks a handler. This tells the next agent where to add a case. Use a binding of type `never` in TypeScript. Use an unannotated `match` in Rust. Use `-Wincomplete-patterns` in Haskell. Use an exhaustive match of sealed classes in Kotlin.
- Derive types from the schema that owns their shape. That schema can be a protocol buffer, OpenAPI spec, GraphQL schema, database migration, design-token file, or another source. Do not write a parallel type by hand. See [Encode Lessons in Structure](encode-lessons-in-structure.md).
- Strengthen a type only where a partial case appears. A runtime assertion, null check, or "this should never happen" throw shows that the type is too weak. Move that check into the type. Then stop. The type system tracks the cases that each use site must handle. It need not describe the data as precisely as possible. Prefer total functions. `sum` of an empty list is 0, so it accepts a plain list. `head` of an empty list has no answer. It requires a non-empty list. Keep the plain type when nothing would otherwise panic.
